name: Inositol

track.title: Pilot in people
track.line: No energy or fat-loss injection studies found

what.text: Inositol is a small molecule the body uses in cell signalling. It is sometimes called a pseudovitamin: the body needs it, but a lack of it does not cause a recognized deficiency disease. It is the “I” in “MIC” injections.

src.label: PubChem (NIH National Library of Medicine), inositol record

research.text: We found no published human study of injected inositol, alone or in MIC blends, for energy or fat loss.

us.text: We found no FDA-approved inositol product. Using inositol injections for energy or weight loss is not an approved use.
A search of FDA’s Drugs@FDA data for inositol as an active ingredient returned no approved product.

src.label: Drugs@FDA data search for inositol (FDA, openFDA)

us.text: FDA lists inositol as nominated for outsourcing-facility (503B) compounding and “under evaluation” (Category 1). FDA’s 503A lists name only a different substance, inositol hexanicotinate, in Category 3 (nominated without adequate support).

src.label: FDA, Bulk drug substances nominated under section 503B (categories)
FDA, Bulk drug substances nominated under section 503A (categories)

us.text: Compounded drugs are not FDA approved. That includes compounded MIC and lipotropic injection blends containing inositol.

src.label: FDA, Compounding and the FDA: Q&A

us.text: FDA’s recall records list many compounded “lipotropic”, “Lipo-B” and methionine/inositol/choline (MIC) injections recalled by compounding pharmacies, most often for “lack of assurance of sterility.” Examples: Isomeric Pharmacy Solutions’ cyanocobalamin/methionine/inositol/choline vials (2017), Partell Specialty Pharmacy’s MIC + B12 vials (2018), Assurance Infusion’s Lipo B vials (2020) and Tailor Made Compounding’s MIC + B12 + carnitine vials (2022). These were recalls of specific pharmacies’ lots, not a ruling on the ingredients.

world.lead: We found no approved inositol medicine in the US or on EMA’s central list. Other countries were not checked.

after.title: Sport
after.text: Inositol is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or on the 2027 List, which takes effect January 1, 2027. Separately, the lists' method M2.2 bans intravenous infusions or injections of more than 100 mL per 12-hour period, except in hospital treatment, surgery or clinical tests.

side.text: There is no FDA label for injected inositol, so there is no labelled side-effect list.
FDA’s recall records show compounded MIC injections recalled for lack of assurance of sterility, a risk with any injection made without sterile controls.

unconfirmed: Canada, UK (MHRA), national EU and Australian (TGA) status could not be confirmed from the regulators’ records.
surprises: MIC injections are marketed for fat loss, yet we found no human study of injected inositol for that use and no FDA-approved inositol product.
